paper.title: Principal-Agent Bandit Games with Self-Interested and Exploratory Learning Agents

settings.name_in_paper: Self-interested learning agent, i.i.d. reward setting
unmapped: Principal-agent game: principal offers incentive vector, agent chooses arm maximizing its empirical mean plus incentive (greedy learning agent)
Principal observes chosen arm and own reward only; agent's rewards hidden
Regret measured against per-round optimal incentive (time-varying benchmark depending on agent's empirical means)
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, the agent selects an arm $A_t$ that maximizes the empirical mean plus an incentive proposed by the principal: $A_t \in \argmax_{a} \{\hatmu_a(t)+\pi_a(t)\}$ ... the reward of each arm $a$ for the principal is drawn from a $[0,1]$-bounded distribution

settings.name_in_paper: Exploratory learning agent, i.i.d. reward setting
unmapped: Principal-agent game with incentives; agent plays empirical maximizer of mean+incentive except with exploration probability p_t <= c0 sqrt(log(2t)/t), exploring arbitrarily
Principal knows the exploration bound function c0 sqrt(log(2t)/t)
settings.definition_quote: Let the probability that agent explores at round $t$ be $p_t = \P(A_t \notin \argmax_{a} \{\hatmu_a(t)+\pi_a(t)\})$. There exists a absolute constant $c_0 \geq 0$ such that $p_t \leq c_0 \sqrt{t^{-1}\log(2t)}$

settings.name_in_paper: Exploratory oracle-agent (agent model of Dogan et al. 2023), i.i.d. reward
unmapped: Principal-agent game; agent selects true maximizer of mean+incentive when not exploring, explores with probability p_t <= c0 sqrt(log(2t)/t)
Regret measured by bar R_T of Dogan et al.: max_b(theta_b+mu_b) - max_z mu_z - (theta_{A_t} - sum_a pi_a(t))
settings.definition_quote: When we reduce the learning behavior in Definition 2.1 to the exploratory oracle-agent considered by (dogan2023estimating) ... we adopt $\E[\overline{R}_T]$

settings.name_in_paper: Self-interested learning agent, linear reward setting
unmapped: Principal-agent game; agent estimates its parameter by OLS and plays argmax of <s_hat_t,a> + incentive
Two unknown parameters s* (agent) and nu* (principal), both in unit ball
settings.definition_quote: We assume $\calA \subseteq B(0,1)$ ... $\calA$ spans $\fR^d$. The reward observed by the agent is $R_{A_t}(t)=\inner{s^\star,A_t}+\eta^A(t)$, and the reward on the principal side is $X_{A_t}(t)= \inner{\nu^\star,A_t}+\eta^P(t)$ where $s^\star,\nu^\star \in B(0,1)$ ... conditionally $1$-subgaussian.

algorithms.name: Algorithm 1 (elimination with noisy binary search with asymmetric check)
Algorithm for self-interested learning agent with exploration (alg:explore_agent)
Algorithm for self-interested oracle-agent with exploration (alg:explore_oracle_agent)
Algorithm for linear reward model with multiscale Steiner potential conservative cut (alg:linear_alg)

source.label: thm:main_result_MAB
source.quote: By choosing $\delta=T^{-1}$ for \pref{alg:MAB_alg}, we have $\E[R_T] = \order \big(K\log^2 T+\sqrt{KT\log(KT)}\big)$.

results.notes: Regret is against per-round optimal incentive utility (time-varying benchmark); quantity mapped to pseudo_regret since defined via principal means theta and expectations. Comparator mapping approximate.

source.label: thm:main_result_exploration
source.quote: Suppose $T=\Omega(K)$. Choosing $\delta=1/T$ for \pref{alg:explore_agent} ensures $\E[R_T]=\order  \big( \big(K\log^2 T\big)^{1/3}  T^{2/3} \big).$

results.notes: Agent exploration probability bounded by c0 sqrt(log(2t)/t); proof shows additional lower-order terms absorbed.
Regret measured by bar R_T of Dogan et al. (benchmark max(theta+mu) - max mu, subtracting total incentives). Improves Dogan et al.'s T^{11/12}.

conditions: action set spans R^d, contained in unit ball

source.label: thm:main_result_linear
source.quote: Suppose $T=\Omega(d)$. By choosing $\delta=T^{-1}$ in \pref{alg:linear_alg}, we have that $\E[R_T]= \order \big(d^{\frac{4}{3}}T^{\frac{2}{3}}\log^{\frac{2}{3}}(KT) \big)$.

results.notes: K is the (finite) number of arms; proof has lower-order d^{3/2}sqrt(T) log and d^2 log^3 terms. Volume-based search step computational cost not discussed.

source.label: thm:comparison_result_exploration
source.quote: Suppose $T=\Omega(K)$. By choosing $\delta=1/T$, \pref{alg:explore_agent} ensures \[ \E[\overline{R}_T]  =\order \rbr{  \log^{\frac{5}{3}} (KT) K^{\frac{1}{3}} T^{\frac{2}{3}} +  \log^{2} (KT) \sqrt{KT} +K^2\log^3(KT) }.\]

results.notes: Measured with Dogan et al.'s regret bar R_T rather than R_T; setting assignment (exploratory learning agent) inferred from algorithm used.
